claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can be maintained as a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy in the proposed regime.
HfNbTaTiZr has a thermal conductivity of approximately 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
The low thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr is caused by lattice distortion and defect scattering.
Point defects specifically are an important source of scattering in the initial HfNbTaTiZr state.
Annealing below the order-disorder transition and above the onset of clustering can evolve SRO from isolated clusters into a percolating network.
Breaking local chemical order can create a diffuse antiphase boundary with an associated enthalpic cost.
A suitable potential energy surface for modeling HfNbTaTiZr must reproduce the enthalpic cost of disrupting SRO.
SRO is stable without complete ordering in the proposed temperature range of 800–1100 K.
The potential energy surface must capture SRO-induced changes in phonon dispersion rather than only mass disorder.
At low SRO volume fractions, isolated SRO clusters reduce thermal conductivity by acting as strong phonon-scattering centers.
Above a critical percolation threshold, connected SRO clusters form coherent, low-scattering phonon-transport pathways.
The percolating ordered matrix reduces the effective scattering volume fraction for selected phonon modes.
Percolation of SRO suppresses diffuse-antiphase-boundary scattering that dominates in the isolated-cluster regime.
A connected SRO matrix increases phonon mean free path and thereby increases thermal conductivity.
SRO flattens the energy landscape for edge dislocations and enhances their mobility in MoNbTaW.
Thermal conductivity will pass through a minimum at intermediate SRO volume fraction and then increase significantly after SRO percolation.
Serial/parallel mixing models and mass-disorder-only Debye–Callaway models predict a monotonic decrease in thermal conductivity as SRO increases.
Long-range phase separation or precipitation would introduce additional interface or grain-boundary scattering that could negate the proposed percolative effect.
Cr-Hf is the most strongly attractive pair among those examined in a W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf refractory alloy.

The proposed transition from scattering-dominated to pathway-dominated phonon transport has not been experimentally verified in bcc refractory high-entropy alloys and is inferred from dislocation-mobility studies.
